absence: The sheet gives scenarios with watchpoints. It names no LOB or status, so none is recorded. origin names who proposed each one.

focusItems.whyItMatters: An aircraft or component previously designed, maintained or repaired by CA is subsequently involved in a major accident or incident, exposing CA to investigation and potential litigation.
focusItems.impact: Safety and reputational impact; investigations and litigation; potential financial exposure from claims.

focusItems.focus: Cyberattack (including AI driven) resulting in data breach
focusItems.whyItMatters: A major cyberattack compromises CA systems or information and disrupts business operations.
focusItems.impact: Operational disruption; information compromise; regulatory/compliance and financial exposure.
indicators: Cyber threat and security incidents, including increased attacks on critical providers, especially within the industry

focusItems.whyItMatters: Escalating geopolitical tensions drive technology bifurcation and tighter export controls, restricting CA’s ability to transfer technology or ship products and parts between key markets.
focusItems.impact: Shipment stoppages; technology/supply constraints; operational disruption; inventory build-up and market-access constraints.
indicators: Geopolitical developments and introduction of new policies
export-control/licensing expiring with no renewal and technology/IP restrictions
supply-chain separation by OEMs/suppliers for different markets

focusItems.focus: Geopolitical fragmentation prolongs supply and cost disruption
focusItems.whyItMatters: Escalating conflicts and trade tensions bring sanctions, export controls, tariffs and route disruption, causing critical material shortages; OEMs and single-source suppliers tighten access to parts, technical data, repair rights and licences; longer lead times, rising input and energy costs and missed TAT occur while customers resist cost pass-through, squeezing margins and working capital.
focusItems.relevantRisks: Geopolitics & protectionism; OEM / single-source dependency; Legal & trade compliance; Pricing pressure; Customer credit; FX & interest rates.
indicators: Political developments in regions key to the aerospace supply chain
critical parts with no qualified alternative, especially at Tier 2 and Tier 3
spikes in lead times, freight and energy costs, or minimum-order requirements
higher OEM licensing, royalty, repair-right or technical-data costs
new or changing sanctions, embargoes, export controls or tariffs affecting customers, suppliers or countries of operation

focusItems.focus: Aviation growth collides with capacity, talent and customer stress
focusItems.whyItMatters: Demand stays strong, but technician shortages, long training and certification lead times, and supplier delays cap throughput; price-sensitive customers under fuel and margin pressure seek longer payment terms and some face liquidity issues; resulting impacts include weaker competitiveness, delivery delays, margin erosion, higher receivables and reliance on a few key customers.
focusItems.relevantRisks: Pricing competition; Technical talent shortage; Customer credit; Customer concentration; Quality & regulatory compliance; Supply-chain dependency.
indicators: Customers pushing for delays, renegotiation or cost absorption
whether cost pass-through and force-majeure clauses hold up in practice
labour-market trends from external HR vendors
emerging technology and its impact on skills required
